seeds.title: Adopt a shared confirmation policy matrix
seeds.statement: Define a cross-surface action policy matrix spanning Orchestrator runtime, Source Control, cleanup, and governance flows, using explicit confirmation levels and reversibility classes.
evidence: Docs currently have isolated confirmations but no unified action policy.
Recommended matrix axes are confirmation level and reversibility class.

seeds.title: Standardize confirmation levels
seeds.statement: Classify user actions into none, light, strong, and hard_gate confirmation levels so risk handling is consistent and predictable.
evidence: Candidate levels are listed as none, light, strong, and hard_gate.
Current behavior is fragmented across multiple feature-specific rules.

seeds.title: Differentiate undoability from compensation
seeds.statement: Model reversibility separately as immediate_undo, compensating_action_only, and non_reversible, and expose recovery paths that match real system capabilities.
evidence: Recommended reversibility classes separate true undo from compensating actions.
Many orchestration actions are explicitly not true editor-style undo operations.

seeds.title: Reserve hard gates for contract-controlled approvals
seeds.statement: Use hard_gate only when runtime or HITL contracts define allowed actions, and prevent bypass through generic confirmation modals.
evidence: Hard-gated actions are described as canonical approval/blocked flows that cannot be bypassed.
HITL approvals already rely on explicit allowed actions instead of generic confirms.

seeds.title: Enrich strong confirmation payloads
seeds.statement: Strong confirmations should include target scope, concrete consequences, artifact/history impact, and reversibility class rather than generic yes/no prompts.
evidence: Strong confirm guidance calls for target objects, consequence summary, retention details, and reversibility.
Docs explicitly warn against generic 'Are you sure?' confirmations.

seeds.title: Use precise recovery language
seeds.statement: Normalize action copy so Undo is used only for true immediate undo, while Reopen, Restore, Retry from Safe Point, and Create New Lane are used for compensating flows.
evidence: Recommended labels distinguish Undo from Reopen/Restore/Retry/New Lane.
The notes emphasize avoiding over-promising undo when only compensation exists.

seeds.title: Apply strict confirmation to destructive cleanup
seeds.statement: Worktree prune/remove, workspace cleanup, and evidence pruning should require strong confirmation with explicit disclosure of lineage retention and restore limitations.
evidence: Destructive cleanup actions are mapped into strong confirmation guidance.
Docs require disclosure of worktree removal, lineage retention, and direct restore availability.

seeds.title: Treat authorization separately from confirmation
seeds.statement: Do not conflate UI confirmation with permission: high-consequence runtime actions should bind to blocked/HITL contracts where authorization is enforced by runtime policy.
evidence: Docs state confirmation is not equivalent to authorization.
High-consequence runtime actions are recommended to bind to canonical blocked/HITL contracts.

seeds.title: Finalize delete-run semantics before enabling deletion
seeds.statement: History delete actions should remain constrained until deletion semantics, reversibility, and recovery guarantees are explicitly defined in the shared policy.
evidence: Delete Run is called out as questionable pending clearer reversibility semantics.
Current terminology and policy inconsistencies create high risk for misleading destructive actions.

seeds.title: Define canonical record family envelopes
seeds.statement: Specify normalized record envelopes and linkage for review, corroboration, graph patch, promotion, recovery, and state-transition records, with Ledger as exact record authority and projections for summary views.
evidence: Major record families are named but still under-shaped compared with established attempt/blocked/usage families.
Docs state exact records belong in Ledger while summary and inspection surfaces may project from them.
